To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The fundamental limits of user-privacy in the presence of obfuscation and anonymization mechanisms are determined by the obfuscation and anonymity parameters, as well as the number of time series samples.”

(1) the privacy of a user is compromised if the obfuscation level is too low; (2) the privacy is compromised if the anonymization level is too low or too high; (3) there is a tradeoff between privacy and user utility; (4) the tradeoff between the privacy and utility can be improved if the anonymization mechanism is designed carefully; and (5) the obfuscation mechanism has a negligible effect on the tradeoff.
the fundamental limits of anonymization-based privacy protection mechanisms are characterized by the tradeoff between the amount of obfuscation and the number of users.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental limits of privacy in time series data, and provides a framework to evaluate the tradeoff between user privacy and user utility.
the fundamental limits of privacy for time-series data and the corresponding tradeoff between privacy and user utility.
the theoretical limits of privacy protection in a scenario where user traces are anonymized and then obfuscated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fundamental limits of privacy protection in this context are well understood and are achievable by the obfuscation and anonymization mechanisms we propose.
the obfuscation and anonymization planes have a unique intersection, and that the region of the plane above this intersection corresponds to the region of perfect user privacy.
the obfuscation/anonymization plane can indeed be divided into two disjoint regions: in one region all users have perfect anonymity; in the second region none of them has any privacy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we derive the fundamental bounds for privacy of users when anonymization and obfuscated time-series data are used.

the fundamental limits of privacy in the presence of both anonymization and data obfuscation are characterized by the following two parameters: (1) the number of users and (2) the number of time samples per user.
the privacy of a user can only be protected if there is a significant amount of obfuscation in addition to anonymization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the privacy of a user can be compromised by statistical matching techniques even in the presence of obfuscation and anonymization mechanisms.
, for a given user utility level, there is a threshold number of users above which all users have perfect protection and below which no user can be protected.
, in order for a user to have any privacy, the obfuscator needs to introduce a certain level of noise in the data.
